[Q1.] What is a "solar cell"?
A solar cell (also called photovoltaic or PV) converts sunlight directly into electricity. A single, discrete unit of this technology can be referred to as a 'photovoltaics' and it's also known by its acronym: P.V.. The term ‘PV’ refers both to an individual module that produces power from light energy in addition to all systems associated with generating electrical current using photo-voltaic cells such as arrays for residential use which may include batteries too!
The process begins when photons strike atoms within silicon wafers causing electrons inside them become excited enough so they jump out onto another layer where these free moving particles create electric currents through wires connected at either end - thus producing usable DC voltage output capable powering devices like lights bulbs etc..

There are three animals in an enclosure. They can't see each other or hear each other.
The first animal is either a cat or not-a-cat with equal probability; if it's a cat then there will be no more information given to you.
If this animal isn't a cat, they'll tell you whether the second animal is a cat or a dog - but only after telling you that!
Then the third animal tells you what kind of creature he/she/it is... again, only after hearing from both previous creatures! What do these last two say?
This problem was posed by my friend Tom Leinster on Google+. He got some interesting answers , including mine . But I want to talk here mainly because his post led me into another fun game involving probabilities...
Let A = "the first animal", C = "a cat" and D = "not a cat". Then we have four possibilities for our world W :
W1 : ACACD
W2 : ACCCD
W3 : ADADDD
W4 : ADDDC
We're told P(Wi) = ¼ .
Now let X denote whatever happens when the second animal speaks up. We know nothing at all until she/he says something, so initially we must assume P(X|Wi)=0 for any possible value of X ! This means P(A,C,X,Wi) = P(C,A,X)|P(Wi). So,

But since CCXX has zero probability unless XX=CXCXDCCDXCDDD ,

hole is a region of space from which nothing, including light , can escape. The theory that such regions exist was first developed in the 18th century by John Michell and Pierre-Simon Laplace . Either an object falling into a black hole will go through the event horizon (the boundary marking its surface) without noticing it or else be torn apart at this point.
Astronomers have not yet detected direct evidence for their existence; however, there are indirect methods to detect them: they may produce observable effects on surrounding matter due to gravitational lensing ; accretion disks around compact objects like neutron stars might behave differently than those orbitting black holes because of quantum mechanical processes near the latter's horizons .
The term "black hole" has been used since about 1967 when physicist Robert H. Dicke coined it as part of his research program investigating whether gravity could cause singularities where all known laws break down - something he called 'gravitational collapse'. In modern usage though we usually mean any type II singularity with infinite density but finite size rather just one specific kind so named after being discovered independently several times over history under different names depending upon what properties were considered most important e.g., Schwarzschild radius etc..

0=m(a + g)
=>(a/g)=(-1).
